explanations: luna: The section's dictionary form says a mount may *qāmat* when it tires and stops moving; here people walk when light appears but قَامُوا when darkness returns, a halt on an uncertain route.
terra: When divine guidance comes, whoever follows it will neither go astray nor grieve; the dependent traveller’s safety is made conditional on following guidance.

luna: The section's *nasta'in* is a request for aid; this command says وَاسْتَعِينُوا بِالصَّبْرِ وَالصَّلَاةِ, naming patience and prayer as supports to seek. | terra: “Seek help through patience and prayer” gives the section’s نَسْتَعِينُ concrete supports for a weakened traveller.
luna: The section's image depends on help from another person; this warning about the Day of Recompense says no soul can avail another and وَلا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ, setting a limit on human aid.
luna: Ibrahim and Ismail raise the House's foundations, يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ الْقَوَاعِدَ, then ask God to accept their work; two people build a lasting support and turn to God for aid.
luna: After the foundation-building in 2:127, Ibrahim and Ismail ask God to show them their rites, وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا; this ayah's own contribution is a request for guidance in worship.

luna: The section's root ع و ن appears again in وَاسْتَعِينُوا بِالصَّبْرِ وَالصَّلَاةِ; this repeated command names patience and prayer as aid to seek and adds God's presence with the patient. | terra: Again commands believers to seek help through patience and prayer, adding that God is with the patient when endurance is needed.

luna: The ayah includes the wayfarer, وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ, among those who receive wealth in a definition of righteousness; it gives the stranded traveler's need a concrete place in the community's care.
terra: Believers are shaken by adversity until they ask when God’s help will come; the answer that it is near gives requested aid a crisis scene.
luna: The answer about charitable spending includes وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ among its recipients, giving the section's traveler in need a place in a list of people others must support.

luna: The command وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قَانِتِينَ places upright bodily standing inside worship, joining the section's movement from serving God to seeking aid. | terra: Standing devoutly before God in prayer makes the source’s q-w-m bodily uprightness part of worship itself.
terra: Facing Goliath, the believers ask for patience to be poured on them, firm feet, and help: a prayer for standing rather than collapsing.

luna: The section's q-w-m dictionary branch glosses *qiyām* as a prop or support; the divine name الْقَيُّومُ presents God as the one who sustains all, a broader scale of that support. | terra: The source’s q-w-m dictionary sense of a sustaining pillar meets al-Qayyūm, the ever-sustaining ground of the traveller’s reliance.

luna: The section describes help as what one leans on; here the believer holds to an unbreakable handhold, الْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقَىٰ, an explicit image of dependable support. | terra: The unbreakable “firm handhold” supplies a visible support under the weak person’s grip.
terra: An indirect but concrete reversal of the stalled mount: a passerby is shown his dead donkey restored, so a stopped journey becomes a sign of renewed life.
luna: The poor described here are restricted in God's way and لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ ضَرْبًا فِي الْأَرْضِ; their inability to move through the land makes need and immobility meet in one scene.

luna: The section's q-w-m dictionary sense is erect standing; here the usurer's rise is likened to one stumbling in a demonic seizure, لَا يَقُومُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَقُومُ الَّذِي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ, a distorted opposite of steady uprightness.

luna: The prayer asks not to be burdened beyond capacity, لَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ, then asks God for victory; it voices dependence and need for help from a place of human weakness. | terra: The closing prayer asks that no soul bear beyond its capacity, then calls God its protector and asks for help.
luna: The section's q-w-m dictionary branch glosses *qiyām* as support; الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ repeats the name of the one who sustains, in a shorter declaration than 2:255.
terra: After receiving guidance, believers ask that their hearts not deviate; the source’s swaying walker becomes inward instability held by mercy.
luna: The section names root ق و م in *mustaqīm* and makes uprightness bodily; Zakariya is قَائِمٌ يُصَلِّي in the sanctuary when the angels call him, joining standing posture with worship.

luna: The section names roots ع ب د and ق و م in its worship and straight-path wording; Jesus says worship is the straight path, فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ. | terra: Jesus names worship of the one Lord as the straight path, repeating the source section’s movement from naʿbudu to the requested road.
terra: Jesus asks who will be his helpers toward God, and the disciples answer that they are God’s helpers; aid becomes companions who stand with a messenger.

luna: The section's roots ع و ن (aid) and ه د ي (guidance) meet here: whoever holds fast to God is guided to a straight path, فَقَدْ هُدِيَ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ. | terra: Holding fast to God is followed by being guided to a straight path, joining a secure grip to directed movement.
terra: Holding all together to God’s rope turns the two-sided support of the source’s walker into communal dependence that prevents division.
terra: Two groups are about to lose courage, but God is their protector; it stages a faltering body or community upheld before it gives way.
terra: God promises to reinforce the vulnerable believers with sent-down angels, another answer in which help takes the form of supporting companions.
terra: The angelic reinforcement is made good news so hearts may be reassured; its own contribution is the inner steadiness that aid is meant to give.
terra: The prophets’ followers ask for forgiveness, firm feet, and divine help, directly joining inner repair to upright footing.

luna: The section's dictionary wording says the good walk is not rushed like a defeated person; at Uhud the believers climb away without turning back, إِذْ تُصْعِدُونَ وَلَا تَلْوُونَ عَلَىٰ أَحَدٍ, the explicit fleeing gait that bounds the calm image.
terra: “If God helps you” no one can overcome you, and if He leaves you no one can help: the verse fixes the true source of support.

luna: After believers are warned that enemies have gathered, they say حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ; their reliance on God under threat parallels the section's aid sought when human strength is insufficient. | terra: Threatened believers answer that God is sufficient and the best disposer of affairs, an enacted refusal to seek a less reliable support.

luna: The section names root ق و م in *mustaqīm* and makes uprightness bodily; this ayah names remembrance of God while قِيَامًا وَقُعُودًا وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمْ, standing, sitting, and lying on sides.
terra: The source’s q-w-m family calls qiyām a support; this ayah calls wealth qiyāman for people, a material means by which life stands.
terra: God wants to lighten the burden because the human being was created weak, naming the bodily need that makes help necessary.
luna: The section names root ق و م and glosses *qiyām* as support; this ayah uses قَوَّامُونَ for a sustaining role tied in its own wording to spending, a social form of support.
luna: Among commands to treat others well, this ayah names both وَالصَّاحِبِ بِالْجَنبِ and وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ, joining a companion at one's side with the traveler who needs care.

luna: Oppressed men, women, and children cry to God to bring them out and appoint a protector and helper; their explicit plea for rescue and backing closely matches the section's support-seeking traveler. | terra: The oppressed weak men, women, and children ask God for a guardian and a helper, a direct social form of the assisted traveller.
luna: These people say they were oppressed and weak in the land; the next ayah, 4:98, specifies those unable to find a way, completing the picture of people whose movement is constrained.

luna: The section names root ه د ي and pictures someone too weak to proceed alone; this ayah describes people unable to devise a way or find a path, وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلًا. | terra: The oppressed weak people cannot devise a plan or find a way, directly naming those who need both help and guidance.
luna: The section begins with a traveler stranded when his mount fails; this ayah promises a migrant many places of refuge and ample provision, مُرَاغَمًا كَثِيرًا وَسَعَةً.
terra: Travel permits a shortened prayer under threat, showing worship itself eased for a vulnerable traveller rather than imposed as an added weight.
luna: The section's q-w-m family carries bodily standing; this ayah tells worshippers to remember God standing, sitting, and on their sides, naming the body's changing postures.

luna: The section names q-w-m as the family behind standing upright; كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ applies that standing to a sustained commitment to justice. | terra: The source’s q-w-m uprightness becomes ethical in qawwāmīn for justice, standing firmly even when testimony cuts against oneself.

luna: The section's roots ع و ن and ه د ي join aid to guidance; this ayah joins holding fast to God, وَاعْتَصَمُوا بِهِ, with His guiding people to a straight path. | terra: Those who hold fast to God receive mercy and are guided to a straight path; grasping support and receiving direction occur together.

luna: The section's root ع و ن names aid and helping; وَتَعَاوَنُوا calls believers to support one another in goodness and reverence, extending the two people holding up the weak traveler into shared action. | terra: “Cooperate in righteousness and reverence” makes believers one another’s practical عون, as the source says help is whatever one relies on.

luna: The section's q-w-m image includes bodily straightness; the command كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ لِلَّهِ applies the root to standing firmly as witnesses for justice. | terra: Qawwāmīn for God must not let hatred bend them from justice, extending the source’s upright stance to a moral refusal to swerve.

luna: The section names roots ه د ي and ق و م in asking for guidance to the straight path; this ayah says God guides people through paths of peace and to a straight path, وَيَهْدِيهِمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ. | terra: By the Book, God leads seekers of His approval along paths of peace, out of darkness and onto a straight path.

luna: The section names q-w-m and gives the dictionary gloss *qiyām* as support; the Kaaba is made قِيَامًا لِّلنَّاسِ, a communal support. | terra: The Kaʿbah and sacred ordinances are qiyāman for people; the source’s q-w-m support becomes an institution that steadies a community.

luna: The section's root ه د ي includes a wavering walk and the request for guidance; here a confused person is lost on earth while companions call him to guidance, الْهُدَى, and back to the right way. | terra: A bewildered person is driven about on earth while companions call him to guidance; this is the assisted, unsteady traveller reversed by refusing God’s هدًى.
terra: Stars guide travellers through the darknesses of land and sea, giving ihdinā’s guidance a literal wayfinding scene.
terra: One made alive receives a light and walks among people, unlike one trapped in darkness; the image makes guided walking a supported bodily passage.
terra: Guidance opens the breast, while misguidance constricts it; the source’s supported body has an inner counterpart in expanded or compressed capacity.

luna: The section names root ق و م in *mustaqīm*; this command calls God's route the straight path, صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيمًا, and warns against side paths that divide the traveler. | terra: God’s single straight path is to be followed, while other paths split a person away from it; the source’s upright route has a concrete boundary.
terra: The speaker is guided to a straight path described as an upright religion, tightly joining h-d-y to the source’s q-w-m uprightness.
terra: Satan waits on the straight path to obstruct it, the hostile counterpart to the supports sought by the traveller.

luna: Moses tells his people, اسْتَعِينُوا بِاللَّهِ وَاصْبِرُوا; the section's request for help is here joined to patience while facing hardship. | terra: Moses tells his people, “Seek help from God and be patient,” directly pairing istiʿānah with the endurance that keeps them standing.
terra: The believers cry to their Lord for rescue and He answers with angels; requested help is answered by companions sent to reinforce them.
terra: Following the cry for aid in 8:9, this ayah says the angelic response reassures hearts while victory remains from God; it distinguishes the help’s means from its source.

luna: In the battle scene, rain removes hardship, strengthens hearts, and steadies feet, وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ الْأَقْدَامَ; divine aid is pictured as making people physically firm. | terra: God binds their hearts and makes their feet firm; inner fastening and physical footing realize the source’s body being held upright.
terra: God tells the angels to strengthen the believers, another explicit scene of divine helpers bracing those who would otherwise falter.
terra: A few oppressed people afraid of being seized are sheltered, aided, and provided for; help changes exposed weakness into secure standing.
terra: Calling God the excellent protector and excellent helper states the dependable support behind requests for assistance.
luna: The section's story uses قوّة as strength lent to build a protective barrier; here the same word names military force prepared to deter enemies, a specific different use of strength.
luna: God supports the Prophet through believers and brings their hearts together; the verse makes people a source of backing, as in the section's two companions supporting one walker.

luna: The verse pairs emigration with those who gave shelter and aid, وَالَّذِينَ آوَوا وَنَصَرُوا; it depicts travelers being received and supported after leaving home. | terra: Those who give shelter and help to emigrants become allies of those displaced believers, a social realization of the traveller being held up by others.
terra: The later restatement that migrants and those who shelter and help them are true believers preserves mutual support as a defining communal act.

luna: In the cave, the Prophet reassures his companion, لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا; God then sends tranquility and support, joining companionship to aid in distress. | terra: In the cave God sends tranquillity and supports the Prophet with unseen forces, showing aid arriving when a traveller is isolated.
luna: The wayfarer, وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ, is explicitly among those eligible for alms, making communal resources a form of aid for the traveler in need.
luna: Believing men and women are described as allies of one another, أَوْلِيَاءُ بَعْضٍ; this is a specific communal counterpart to the two people supporting the weak walker.
luna: The weak, sick, and resource-less are excused from setting out; this names bodily weakness and inability to travel as a concrete boundary on movement.
terra: Those who come seeking a mount are turned away because none is available; their grief gives the source’s stranded rider a Qur’anic scene.

luna: The section describes a wall about to fall and then repaired; this parable contrasts a building founded on reverence with one on the edge of a crumbling bank that collapses, فَانْهَارَ بِهِ. | terra: A building founded on a crumbling cliff falls with its maker, the opposite of the source’s restored wall and sound support.

luna: After the collapsing-building parable in 9:109, this ayah says the building they made remains a source of doubt in their hearts; it completes the scene with the structure's lasting inner effect.
terra: In the hour of hardship some hearts nearly swerved, yet God turns mercifully toward the Prophet, emigrants, and helpers, preventing inner collapse.
luna: People sailing through a storm call to God to save them, دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ; this is another traveler dependent on a conveyance who seeks aid when it fails.

luna: The section names root ه د ي for guidance and ق و م in *mustaqīm*; God calls to the Home of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path, picturing guidance as leading a traveler to a destination.
terra: God, who guides to truth, is contrasted with one unable to guide unless first guided; it tests which leader a dependent traveller should follow.
terra: After Moses and Aaron pray, they are told to remain steadfast; a plea for God’s action becomes an instruction to stand straight.
luna: The section's dictionary gloss calls *qiyām* a pillar/support; Lot longs for a رُكْنٍ شَدِيدٍ, a strong refuge-pillar, when he cannot protect his guests alone.
terra: Shuʿayb says his success is only through God and that he relies on Him, naming reliance as the condition of acting rightly.
luna: The section's q-w-m image concerns what stands securely; this account contrasts a town still قائم with one reaped down, وَحَصِيدٌ, making standing and collapse neighboring conditions.
terra: “Be steadfast as commanded” gives mustaqīm its standing force, asking the messenger and companions to maintain an upright course.
terra: After 11:112’s command to stand firm, this ayah forbids inclining toward wrongdoers and warns that no protector or help remains there.

luna: After the brothers' false account and bloodied shirt, Jacob says وَاللَّهُ الْمُسْتَعَانُ; the section's root ع و ن appears as help sought from God when human reports cannot be relied on. | terra: Jacob’s “beautiful patience” and “God is the One whose help is sought” directly join the source’s istiʿānah to endurance under shock.
terra: Jacob again answers loss with “beautiful patience,” extending 12:18’s supported endurance into a second, renewed deprivation.

luna: The section's dictionary form *qiyām* is a visible prop or support; this ayah describes the heavens raised without pillars that people can see, بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا, a specific boundary between visible props and unseen support.

luna: The section's dictionary entry calls the heart the body's *milāk* or support; this ayah says hearts find rest, تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ, through God's remembrance, an inner steadiness rather than bodily structure.
terra: The messengers admit their human likeness and say believers should rely on God, grounding prophetic action in received favor rather than personal sufficiency.

luna: The section names root ه د ي for guidance; here speakers ask why they should not rely on God after He has guided them to their ways, وَقَدْ هَدَانَا سُبُلَنَا, joining reliance to direction. | terra: The messengers ask why they should not rely on God when He has guided them in their ways: guidance supplies the ground for dependence.
terra: Satan admits that he merely called and cannot rescue those who followed him; it is a false guide and false helper exposed at the end.

luna: The section's dictionary example has a tree standing on its roots; this good tree has أَصْلُهَا ثَابِتٌ, a fixed root, and branches rising upward, making rooted stability visible. | terra: The source’s q-w-m tree image is explicit here: a good word is a tree with roots firmly fixed and branches raised.

luna: The section's tree example emphasizes standing on roots; this next ayah says the good tree yields its fruit continually, تُؤْتِي أُكُلَهَا كُلَّ حِينٍ, showing what rooted stability sustains (14:24 gives the fixed-root image).

luna: The section's tree stands on its roots; the contrary tree is uprooted, اجْتُثَّتْ, with مَا لَهَا مِن قَرَارٍ, no stable place to remain. | terra: The evil word is an uprooted tree with no stability, reversing the source’s standing tree rooted in support.
terra: God makes believers firm by the firm word in this life and the next, turning rootedness into sustained human uprightness.

luna: The section begins with a mount that tires or is injured; this ayah shows the ordinary service that such a failure interrupts: livestock carry people's burdens to distant places otherwise reached only with hardship. | terra: Pack animals carry human burdens to lands people could reach only with hardship, directly answering the source’s exhausted rider and mount.
luna: Horses, mules, and donkeys are provided لِتَرْكَبُوهَا; this identifies the normal ride whose exhaustion or injury strands the section's traveler.
terra: The direction of the way belongs to God and some paths are crooked; this supplies a divine measure for the straight route requested in 1:6.

luna: The mountains prevent the earth from shaking, أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ, and the verse names rivers and paths; stable ground and a route are provided together. | terra: Mountains keep earth from swaying with people, while rivers and paths are made so they may be guided; stable footing and wayfinding are paired.
terra: Landmarks and stars guide people, a second literal navigation scene for the traveller who cannot find the way alone.
terra: God brings down the roof of plotters’ building from its foundations, a collapse that clarifies what the raised wall of 18:77 resists.
luna: The section's weak traveler depends on two people; this parable depicts a man unable to act and wholly dependent on his master, then contrasts him with one on a straight path.
terra: The Spirit brings revelation to strengthen believers, explicitly naming it both guidance and good news; the guide fortifies the one who receives it.

luna: The section hears uprightness in the q-w-m family of *mustaqīm*; this ayah says the Qur'an guides to أَقْوَمُ, what is most upright, joining guidance to uprightness. | terra: The Qur’an guides to what is aqwam, joining the source’s h-d-y request to q-w-m’s most upright and sound condition.
luna: The command to give the wayfarer his due, وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ, supplies a social counterpart to the section's stranded traveler: his need creates a right to others' help.
luna: When unable to give the requested material help, the addressee is told to answer with قَوْلًا مَّيْسُورًا; this adds a humane response for the person whose need cannot be met.

luna: The command not to walk arrogantly, وَلَا تَمْشِ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَحًا, opposes the section's measured, unhurried walk; this ayah adds that human strength cannot pierce earth or reach the mountains in height. | terra: The command not to walk exultantly on earth bounds the source’s calm, well-guided gait by rejecting proud strutting.
terra: God made the Prophet firm; without that support he would have inclined a little. It is the source’s swaying body steadied from collapse.

luna: The prayer asks for truthful entry and exit and for a supporting authority from God, سُلْطَانًا نَّصِيرًا; it joins movement along a way with requested backing. | terra: The prayer for a truthful entrance and exit asks God for “supporting authority,” making divine backing accompany every movement through a passage.

luna: The youths ask God for mercy and sound direction in their affair, رَشَدًا; their plea for right guidance in a vulnerable situation meets the section's request for help and a way. | terra: The cave youths ask for mercy and for right guidance in their affair, a compact prayer for the help and direction of a vulnerable group.

luna: The section links bodily support with standing upright; here God makes the youths' hearts firm, وَرَبَطْنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ, when they rise, إِذْ قَامُوا, to declare their faith. | terra: God binds the youths’ hearts when they stand up; fastening the inner support and standing bodily meet in one scene.
terra: After their withdrawal, the youths are promised mercy and ease in their affair; it completes the aid requested in 18:10.
terra: Whom God guides is guided, and one He leaves astray has no guiding protector; the verse makes guidance inseparable from sustaining patronage.
terra: After forgetting, the Prophet asks that his Lord guide him to what is nearer to right conduct, a precise request for corrected direction.
terra: The ruined garden owner has no group to help him against God and cannot defend himself, exposing support that disappears when it is most needed.

luna: Moses names the strain of travel, نَصَبًا, and asks his companion for food; the ayah gives a concrete Quranic traveler whose journey has left him spent and in need. | terra: Moses and his companion acknowledge fatigue from their journey, an actual travel-weariness before the encounter with the divinely taught servant.
terra: The servant is given mercy and knowledge by God; those gifts make him a divinely supplied guide in the journey that reaches the failing wall.

luna: The section asks for guidance; Moses asks to follow a teacher so he may learn right direction, رُشْدًا, directly presenting a seeker asking to be led and taught. | terra: Moses asks whether he may follow the servant to learn right guidance, staging a traveller who needs another’s taught direction.

luna: The section names root م ل ك and its dictionary sense *milāk*, what keeps a wall cohesive; here a wall about to collapse is set upright, فَأَقَامَهُ. In the same ayah the travelers' request for food is refused, joining withheld human aid to structural repair. | terra: The wall about to collapse is erected. The source’s q-w-m sense of setting upright turns failed cohesion into standing protection.

luna: The people ask for a barrier against the attackers, فَاجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُمْ سَدًّا; adjacent 18:95 supplies the distinct contribution of asking for strength to build it, linking the need for protection to requested aid. | terra: A threatened people ask Dhū al-Qarnayn to make a barrier for them, giving vulnerability a communal, protective form.

luna: The section's *nasta'in* (root ع و ن) means asking for aid; Zülkarneyn says فَأَعِينُونِي بِقُوَّةٍ and asks people to lend strength for a barrier, turning aid into a structure that will stand. | terra: “Help me with strength” produces a rampart; requested assistance becomes the force that makes a standing barrier possible.
terra: Zachariah says his bones have weakened and turns to God in prayer, a concrete bodily weakness that seeks help without self-reliance.

luna: The section names roots ع ب د and ق و م in its worship and straight-path wording; Jesus says to worship God and calls it a straight path, فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ. | terra: Worshipping the one Lord is named the straight path, explicitly tying the section’s naʿbudu to the path that follows it.
terra: Abraham tells his father, “Follow me; I will guide you to a straight path,” making guidance an offered companionship in motion.
luna: God commands, فَاعْبُدْنِي وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ; the section's q-w-m family and worship theme meet in a command to worship and establish prayer.

luna: Moses prays, رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي, asking for his chest to be opened; the section's support image is bodily, and this is a specific request for inward capacity. | terra: Moses asks for an expanded breast, beginning his mission with an inward capacity widened for a weight he cannot carry alone.

luna: Moses asks, وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي, for his task to be made easy; this is a direct request for help to proceed, joined to the bodily plea in 20:25. | terra: “Make my task easy” gives the source’s weak traveller a direct prophetic request for an eased passage.

luna: Moses asks for a helper from his family, وَاجْعَل لِّي وَزِيرًا مِّنْ أَهْلِي; linked 20:31 states what this support should do, strengthen his back. | terra: Moses asks for a minister from his family, making assistance take the form of a companion at his side.
luna: Moses names Aaron as the requested helper, هَارُونَ أَخِي; linked 20:31 makes the bodily support explicit as strengthening his back.

luna: The section pictures a weak person supported at the sides; Musa asks that Aaron strengthen his back, اشْدُدْ بِهِ أَزْرِي, making bodily support the means to carry a task. | terra: “Strengthen my back through him” is the clearest bodily counterpart to the source’s traveller leaning on supports.

luna: Moses asks to share his work with Aaron, وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِي أَمْرِي; linked 20:31 explains the support's effect, strengthening his back for the task. | terra: Making Aaron share the task explains why the helper is sought: burden-bearing becomes a joint work rather than solitary strain.
terra: God tells Moses and Aaron not to fear because He is with them, giving their paired mission an unseen supporting presence.
luna: Earth is made مَهْدًا and routes are laid through it; this joins a supporting surface with a way to travel, the two needs embodied in the section's stranded walker.
terra: When Moses feels fear, God tells him not to fear and assures him of the upper hand, a direct act of stabilizing a shaken servant.
luna: Moses is told to travel by night and make for his people a dry path through the sea, فَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقًا فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَسًا; guidance here opens a route for travelers in danger.
terra: Whoever follows God’s guidance will neither go astray nor suffer; supported following is set against the traveller’s feared loss of way.

luna: Mountains keep the earth from shaking, أَن تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ, while routes are made through it; the verse joins a stable ground to paths for travelers. | terra: Firm mountains prevent the earth from swaying with people, and wide paths are set in it so they may be guided: support against wobbling becomes guidance.

luna: The section names root ع و ن for aid and names the Merciful in its opening; this ayah says وَرَبُّنَا الرَّحْمَٰنُ الْمُسْتَعَانُ, joining its Rahman and help-seeking language. | terra: “Our Lord is the Merciful, the One whose help is sought” reunites the source’s Rabb, Raḥmān, and istiʿānah in one prophetic appeal.

luna: The section's dictionary form *tehādī* describes swaying from side to side; people here appear intoxicated from terror, though they are not. The ayah does not say they walk, so the visual resemblance is uncertain.
terra: One worships God on an edge and turns on his face when tried, a precarious reversal of worship that steadies and directs.
terra: The House is purified for those circling, standing, bowing, and prostrating; beside 22:27’s arriving pilgrims, it supplies the upright worship at journey’s end.
terra: Pilgrims come on foot and on every lean camel from deep passes, bringing fatigued bodies and mounts directly into the journey image.
luna: The section's dictionary sense *qiyām* is a support that prevents collapse; this ayah says God holds the sky lest it fall upon earth, وَيُمْسِكُ السَّمَاءَ أَن تَقَعَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ.
terra: God places no hardship in the religion and is the excellent protector and helper, framing worship as held within divine support.
luna: This ayah names livestock as a source of many benefits and food; 23:22 adds that people are carried on them, completing the mount-as-support image in the section.
luna: This ayah states وَعَلَيْهَا وَعَلَى الْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ: people are carried on livestock and ships, the direct image of a mount supporting a traveler.
terra: The Prophet calls people to a straight path; the verse preserves the guiding voice that the source’s dependent traveller needs.
terra: The Lord is sufficient as both guide and helper, joining h-d-y and aid in the exact roles separated by the source’s image.
terra: The Qur’an is sent in stages to strengthen the Prophet’s heart; the source’s dictionary image of the heart as the body’s support gains a direct Qur’anic counterpart.

luna: The section's dictionary form *hedy-i hasen* describes calm, good walking; the servants of the Merciful are described as يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ هَوْنًا, walking gently on earth. | terra: The servants of the Merciful walk gently upon earth, the Qur’anic counterpart to the source’s calm, beautiful gait.

luna: The servants of the Merciful spend the night سُجَّدًا وَقِيَامًا; the verse places standing bodily posture within worship, one side of the section's 1:5–1:6 movement. | terra: The same servants spend the night prostrating and standing before their Lord; after 25:63, their gentle walk opens into bodily worship.

luna: When the sea blocks the fleeing people, Moses says إِنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ; trust in God and the promise of guidance answer a traveler's apparent dead end. | terra: Trapped before the sea, Moses says his Lord is with him and will guide him; divine presence supplies direction at the moment of no way forward.

luna: The section names root ه د ي for guidance; this ayah asks who guides people in the darknesses of land and sea, مَن يَهْدِيكُمْ, making guidance a need of travelers crossing difficult terrain. | terra: God guides through the darknesses of land and sea and sends the winds of mercy, a literal rescue-guide for disoriented travellers.
terra: God binds Moses’s mother’s heart when grief nearly makes her reveal him, a vivid scene of an inner support preventing a person from giving way.
terra: Setting out toward Midian, Moses asks that his Lord guide him to the right way, a traveller’s explicit need for direction.

luna: At the well, two women hold back their flock because they cannot water it until the shepherds leave and their father is old; 28:24 adds Moses' practical help, while this ayah itself establishes their need.

luna: After watering the women's flock, Moses withdraws into shade and prays, إِنِّي لِمَا أَنزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ. A traveler who has helped others then states his own need before God. | terra: After reaching the water, Moses confesses need for whatever good God sends; the tired traveller’s dependence becomes a prayer.

luna: After Moses' prayer for good in 28:24, one woman comes to him walking with modesty and conveys her father's invitation; this ayah depicts help arriving through another person. | terra: The woman comes walking with modest reserve to answer Moses’s need in 28:24; her gait and her help complete a quiet support scene.

luna: The woman describes Moses as strong and trustworthy and proposes hiring him; after the need and invitation in 28:23–25, this ayah's own contribution is a practical offer of support through work.
luna: The promise سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ gives Musa his brother as strength at his arm, a close bodily counterpart to the section's wavering traveler held up by others.
terra: Even love cannot make a person guided; God alone guides whom He wills, marking the limit of any human companion’s help.
luna: The section joins worship and asking for help; this ayah says to seek provision from God, فَابْتَغُوا عِندَ اللَّهِ الرِّزْقَ, and worship Him, فَاعْبُدُوهُ.
terra: The source’s m-l-k image of failed cohesion is reversed in the spider’s house: false protectors provide the weakest house.
terra: Those who strive for God are guided in His paths; effort is not solitary but answered with routes opened by divine guidance.
luna: The verse commands giving the wayfarer his due, وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ, a repeated Quranic formulation of material support for a traveler.
terra: A human caller cannot guide the blind away from error, a boundary on the outward guide when the traveller cannot receive direction.
terra: Human life moves from weakness to strength and back to weakness; the source’s frail body is a created condition, not an incidental failure.

luna: The section's dictionary form *qiyām* is a prop; this repeated creation description says the heavens have no visible pillars, بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا, while firm mountains keep the earth from shaking.

luna: The section's calm, good gait is bounded by the arrogant walk condemned here, وَلَا تَمْشِ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَحًا. | terra: Do not walk boastfully on earth: the source’s composed gait is clarified by its proud, self-sufficient opposite.

luna: The command وَاقْصِدْ فِي مَشْيِكَ asks for measured walking, closely matching the section's calm, unhurried gait after support. | terra: “Be moderate in your walk” directly gives form to the source’s unhurried, well-guided movement.

luna: Turning oneself to God and holding fast to the firmest handhold, اسْتَمْسَكَ بِالْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقَىٰ, gives the section's bodily leaning a direct image of secure reliance. | terra: Submitting to God while doing good is grasping the firmest handhold, renewing the bodily image of a support that will not fail.
terra: Leaders are made to guide by God’s command after patience and certainty; guidance here arises through endured weakness rather than self-sufficiency.
terra: The Prophet is told to rely on God, who is sufficient as disposer of affairs; reliance is stated as an adequate support for action.

luna: The section makes the traveler's dependence visible; this ayah states the specific relation beneath it: people are فقَرَاءُ إِلَى اللَّهِ, in need of God, while He is free of need. | terra: People are needy of God while God is free of need; the source’s helpless traveller becomes the human condition before its only sufficient support.

luna: Allah holds the heavens and earth so they do not cease, يُمْسِكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ أَن تَزُولَا; this enlarges the section's image of support that prevents collapse. | terra: God holds the heavens and earth lest they slip away, a cosmic enactment of the source’s sustaining, upright support.

luna: The section names roots ع ب د and ق و م in its worship and straight-path wording; the command أَنِ اعْبُدُونِي is identified as the straight path, هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ. | terra: “Worship Me; this is a straight path” explicitly makes worship the road that the source’s naʿbudu asks to be helped along.
luna: The animals are made manageable, and مِنْهَا رَكُوبُهُمْ; the section's exhausted mount is a reversal of this stated riding benefit.
terra: The command to lead the guilty to the path of Hell reverses the life-giving horizon of guidance and warns that being led is not itself salvific.
luna: The section names root ه د ي for guidance; Ibrahim says he is going to his Lord and He will guide him, إِنِّي ذَاهِبٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ, joining travel with reliance on guidance.

luna: The section names root ع ب د through *na'budu* and defines help as what one relies on; this ayah asks whether God is not sufficient for His servant, أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِكَافٍ عَبْدَهُ. | terra: “Is God not sufficient for His servant?” names the sufficiency beneath the servant’s request for aid.
terra: The believing man says, “Follow me; I will guide you to the way of right conduct,” another voiced offer of guidance to a follower.
luna: God provides livestock لِتَرْكَبُوا مِنْهَا; the verse identifies animals as the means carrying a journeyer before the section's mount becomes unable to move.

luna: The section's mount has stopped carrying its traveler; this ayah names reaching one's needs on livestock and being carried on them, وَعَلَيْهَا وَعَلَى الْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ, the support in its working state.
terra: The command to be steadfast toward God turns the source’s mustaqīm from a flat road into an upright, directed human stance.
terra: Thamūd prefer blindness to guidance after being shown it, reversing the weak traveller who accepts help to walk rightly.
terra: Those who say “Our Lord is God” and then stand firm receive descending angels and the assurance not to fear or grieve.
terra: The Prophet is said to guide to a straight path, identifying the prophetic voice through which a seeker of ihdinā receives direction.

luna: The section's traveler needs both ground to walk on and guidance; God makes earth مَهْدًا, a resting-place, and puts paths in it so people may be guided. | terra: God makes paths in the earth so people may be guided, preparing traversable ground for the traveller’s request.

luna: The ayah names ships and livestock as what people ride, مَا تَرْكَبُونَ, the travel support whose failure opens the section's image. | terra: God makes ships and cattle for riding, supplying the mount that the source’s exhausted traveller lacks.

luna: The section opens with a mount that fails its rider; here riders settle upon the backs of ships or animals, لِتَسْتَوُوا عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِ, showing the bodily support the failed mount can no longer give. | terra: When riders settle on their mounts, they remember the One who subjected them, admitting this carrying power is received rather than self-made.

luna: The section names ق و م in *mustaqīm* and describes a person leaning on support; here the command فَاسْتَمْسِكْ بِالَّذِي أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ is followed by the claim that the addressee is on a straight path, joining holding fast to the way. | terra: Holding fast to revelation and being on a straight path joins a secure grip to directed movement.

luna: The section names roots ع ب د and ق و م in its worship and straight-path wording; Jesus says worship is the straight path, فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ. | terra: Worshipping the one Lord is called the straight path, again making service to God the route rather than a separate act.
luna: The section pictures a person leaning on human helpers, while this Judgment Day boundary says no patron can avail another, لَا يُغْنِي مَوْلًى عَن مَّوْلًى شَيْئًا, and none will be helped.
terra: Those who say “Our Lord is God” then stand firm have no fear or grief, a promised outcome for sustained uprightness.

luna: The promise وَيُثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَكُمْ makes God's response to support a concrete one: He firms the feet of those who support His cause, echoing the section's aid that lets a person stand and walk. | terra: If believers support God’s cause, He supports them and makes their feet firm; help is rendered as stable footing.
terra: Those who turn back on their heels after guidance has become clear show the reverse movement of the source’s assisted traveller continuing forward.
terra: God sends tranquillity into believers’ hearts so their faith may increase, giving communal firmness an inward support.
luna: The blind, lame, and sick are excused from battle; the explicit عَرَج, lameness, gives a bodily mobility counterpart to the section's disabled mount and weak walker.
terra: The believing community is likened to a plant that grows strong and stands upon its stalk, extending the rooted, upright body into a community.

luna: The section hears bodily uprightness in *mustaqīm*; the purpose لِيَقُومَ النَّاسُ بِالْقِسْطِ uses the q-w-m family for people standing up for justice, extending uprightness into a public stance. | terra: Book and balance are sent so people may stand for justice; revelation becomes the support by which a people stand upright.
terra: Faith brings mercy and a light in which to walk, making divine support into illumination for actual forward movement.
terra: The source’s dictionary example is Qur’anic here: date palms are left standing on their roots, a literal image of stable uprightness.
luna: This verse describes poor emigrants expelled from homes and property who seek God's bounty; it places people made vulnerable by travel and displacement within a community's responsibility.

luna: Those who received emigrants love them and prefer them over themselves, وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ; the verse shows people becoming another's support. | terra: The settled believers welcome and prefer the emigrants despite their own need, showing support that lets displaced people continue rather than remain stranded.
terra: Those who stand in ranks are like a solidly joined structure; the source’s wall-cohesion image becomes mutual human firmness.
terra: “Be helpers of God” is illustrated by Jesus’s disciples answering his call for helpers, a second explicit model of companions lending strength.
terra: Whoever relies on God finds Him sufficient; this names the support on which the source’s unable traveller can actually lean.
terra: God, Gabriel, righteous believers, and angels are named as backers, turning the source’s two supporting sides into layered help.
terra: Earth is made tractable so people may walk its paths and receive provision, showing terrain itself prepared for a dependent walker.

luna: The section's *mustaqīm* carries bodily uprightness as well as a straight route; this ayah sets one who walks face-down against one who walks سَوِيًّا on a straight path. | terra: The face-down walker is contrasted with one walking upright on a straight path, the section’s two bodily gaits stated outright.
terra: The command for “beautiful patience” repeats Jacob’s phrase in 12:18, making patient composure a continuing discipline under pressure.
luna: This ayah establishes a known right in people's wealth; 70:25 identifies the asker and deprived as recipients, completing the link to the section's person seeking aid.
luna: This ayah identifies the asker and deprived, لِلسَّائِلِ وَالْمَحْرُومِ, as those with a known right in wealth, making aid available to people in need.

luna: The earth is spread as a بِسَاطًا and people are given paths through it; the verse makes the ground itself a support for movement along ways. | terra: God spreads earth as a carpet; 71:20 completes its use as ground on which people traverse broad paths.
terra: The broad paths of 71:20 depend on the spread earth of 71:19, making prepared ground part of guided passage.
terra: Had they remained steadfast on the way, God would have given abundant water; upright persistence on a path receives sustaining provision.
terra: No one can protect the speaker from God and no refuge exists apart from Him, drawing the boundary around every lesser support.
luna: The section hears bodily uprightness in root ق و م and joins it to worship; the command قُمِ اللَّيْلَ calls the Prophet to rise for night devotion.
terra: God knows that the Prophet and believers cannot sustain the full measure of night standing, so He relieves them and commands what is easy of recitation.
luna: The section's traveler needs ground on which to stand and walk; this ayah describes earth as a مِهَادًا, a resting-place prepared for people.
luna: The section's dictionary examples use roots and supports to keep something upright; this ayah calls mountains أَوْتَادًا, pegs that secure a structure.
luna: Against the section's bodily help from others, this account of the Day of Recompense says no soul controls anything for another and الْأَمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ.
terra: God promises to ease the messenger toward ease, a concise divine answer to the source’s passage from strain to supported movement.
luna: The section pictures a weak person needing support; this ayah recalls the Prophet as an orphan whom God sheltered, فَآوَىٰ, a direct instance of aid given to vulnerability.

luna: The section names root ه د ي for guidance and describes the lost, wavering traveler; this ayah says God found the Prophet lost and guided him, فَهَدَىٰ. | terra: God finds the Prophet wandering and guides him, making a person once without a way the recipient of direct divine direction.
luna: The section's weak traveler asks for help; this ayah says God found the Prophet in need and enriched him, وَوَجَدَكَ عَائِلًا فَأَغْنَىٰ.
luna: The command وَأَمَّا السَّائِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ gives a direct boundary on how to receive someone who asks, like the section's person seeking aid.
terra: God removes the burden from the Prophet; 94:3 identifies it as one that weighed down his back, the body’s need for relief.
terra: The burden that weighed on the back gives bodily force to the relief announced in 94:2.
terra: “With hardship comes ease” makes the source’s passage from exhaustion to supported movement a promised pairing.
terra: The repeated ease of 94:6 reinforces the relief paired with hardship in 94:5, rather than leaving the burden as the final state.
terra: Humanity is created in the best taqwīm; this q-w-m form gives the source’s upright body a created, bodily ground.
terra: Being returned to the lowest of the low reverses the upright taqwīm of 95:4, marking how bodily or moral standing can be lost.
